## Your own placement {#your-own-placement .smaller}

::: {.small}
- Rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted, in the workspace or in the browser lab: its last line places your estimate on the curve
- The placement counts the specifications of the curve whose estimate is larger than yours. For the reference specification it is **`r placement_ref`** of `r nrow(curve)`
- The same count places the published result (`r mark_of("OA", "rank") - 0.5`) and the five analysts, from `r min(marks_all$rank[marks_all$id %in% analysts$id]) - 0.5` (FQ1G7) to `r max(marks_all$rank[marks_all$id %in% analysts$id]) - 0.5` (LT39B)
:::

::: {.fragment}
Paste your placement in chat – hold – send on "go".
:::

::: notes
Your turn to be placed. Rerun try underscore spec with the choices that you submitted. The last line of its output is your placement: how many of the hundred and ninety-two specifications of the curve have a larger estimate than yours. For the reference specification it is a hundred and fifty, so most of the curve lies above the model of the paper, because most of the curve holds constant fewer things. The published result sits at a hundred and fifty-two. Two or three minutes, then paste your placement in chat, hold it, and send on go. [go] Look at the range in the chat. Every one of you can now say where your estimate stands among a hundred and ninety-two justifiable alternatives, and that sentence – my estimate sits here among the specifications of the curve, built in this way – is a publishable way to report a robustness check.
:::
